314: 			freed->previous = prev_node;

428: 		free_node = free_node->next;
429: 	}

90:  * Name: mm_addregion
91:  *
92:  * Description:
93:  *   This function adds a region of contiguous memory to the selected heap.
94:  *
95:  * Input Parameters:
96:  *   heap      - The selected heap
97:  *   heapstart - Start of the heap region
98:  *   heapsize  - Size of the heap region
99:  *
100:  * Returned Value:
101:  *   None
102:  *
103:  * Assumptions:
104:  *
105:  ****************************************************************************/
106: 
107: void mm_addregion(FAR struct mm_heap_s *heap, FAR void *heapstart,
108:                   size_t heapsize)
109: {
110:   FAR struct mm_freenode_s *node;
111:   uintptr_t heapbase;
112:   uintptr_t heapend;
113:   bool bypass;
114: #if CONFIG_MM_REGIONS > 1
115:   int idx;
116: 
117:   DEBUGVERIFY(nxrmutex_lock(&heap->mm_lock));
118:   bypass = kasan_bypass(true);
119: 
120:   idx = heap->mm_nregions;
121: 
122:   /* Writing past CONFIG_MM_REGIONS would have catastrophic consequences */
123: 
124:   DEBUGASSERT(idx < CONFIG_MM_REGIONS);
125:   if (idx >= CONFIG_MM_REGIONS)
126:     {
127:       kasan_bypass(bypass);
128:       DEBUGVERIFY(nxrmutex_unlock(&heap->mm_lock));
129:       return;
130:     }
131: 
132: #else
133: #  define idx 0
134:   DEBUGVERIFY(nxrmutex_lock(&heap->mm_lock));
135:   bypass = kasan_bypass(true);
136: #endif
137: 
138: #if defined(CONFIG_MM_SMALL) && !defined(CONFIG_SMALL_MEMORY)
139:   /* If the MCU handles wide addresses but the memory manager is configured
140:    * for a small heap, then verify that the caller is  not doing something
141:    * crazy.
142:    */
143: 
144:   DEBUGASSERT(heapsize <= MMSIZE_MAX + 1);
145: #endif
146: 
147: #ifdef CONFIG_MM_FILL_ALLOCATIONS
148:   /* Use the fill value to mark uninitialized user memory */
149: 
150:   memset(heapstart, MM_INIT_MAGIC, heapsize);
151: #endif
152: 
153:   /* Adjust the provided heap start and size.
154:    *
155:    * Note: (uintptr_t)node + MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE is what's actually
156:    * returned to the malloc user, which should have natural alignment.
157:    * (that is, in this implementation, MM_MIN_CHUNK-alignment.)
158:    */
159: 
160:   heapbase = MM_ALIGN_UP((uintptr_t)heapstart + 2 * MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE) -
161:              2 * MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE;
162:   heapsize = MM_ALIGN_DOWN(heapsize - (heapbase - (uintptr_t)heapstart));
163: 
164:   /* Register KASan for access rights check. We need to register after
165:    * address alignment.
166:    */
167: 
168:   if (!heap->mm_nokasan)
169:     {
170:       kasan_register((void *)heapbase, &heapsize);
171:     }
172: 
173:   heapend  = MM_ALIGN_DOWN((uintptr_t)heapbase + (uintptr_t)heapsize);
174:   heap->mm_regionsize[idx] = heapsize;
175:   heapsize = heapend - heapbase;
176: 
177: #if defined(CONFIG_FS_PROCFS) && \
178:     !defined(CONFIG_FS_PROCFS_EXCLUDE_MEMINFO) && \
179:     (defined(CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT) || defined(__KERNEL__))
180:   minfo("[%s] Region %d: base=%p size=%zu\n",
181:         heap->mm_procfs ? heap->mm_procfs->name : "unknown",
182:         idx + 1, heapstart, heapsize);
183: #else
184:   minfo("Region %d: base=%p size=%zu\n", idx + 1, heapstart, heapsize);
185: #endif
186: 
187:   /* Add the size of this region to the total size of the heap */
188: 
189:   heap->mm_heapsize += heapsize;
190: 
191:   /* Create two "allocated" guard nodes at the beginning and end of
192:    * the heap.  These only serve to keep us from allocating outside
193:    * of the heap.
194:    *
195:    * And create one free node between the guard nodes that contains
196:    * all available memory.
197:    */
198: 
199:   heap->mm_heapstart[idx]          = (FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *)heapbase;
200:   MM_RECORD(heap, heap->mm_heapstart[idx]);
201:   heap->mm_heapstart[idx]->size    = MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE | MM_ALLOC_BIT;
202:   node                             = (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)
203:                                      (heapbase + MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE);
204:   DEBUGASSERT((((uintptr_t)node + MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE) % MM_ALIGN) == 0);
205:   node->size                       = heapsize - 2 * MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE;
206:   heap->mm_heapend[idx]            = (FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *)
207:                                      (heapend - MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE);
208:   heap->mm_heapend[idx]->size      = MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE | MM_ALLOC_BIT |
209:                                      MM_PREVFREE_BIT;
210:   heap->mm_heapend[idx]->preceding = node->size;
211:   MM_RECORD(heap, heap->mm_heapend[idx]);
212: 
213: #undef idx
214: 
215: #if CONFIG_MM_REGIONS > 1
216:   heap->mm_nregions++;
217: #endif
218: 
219:   /* Add the single, large free node to the nodelist */
220: 
221:   mm_addfreechunk(heap, node);
222:   heap->mm_curused += 2 * MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE;
223:   sched_note_heap(NOTE_HEAP_ADD, heap, heapstart, heapsize,
224:                   heap->mm_curused);
225: 
226:   kasan_bypass(bypass);
227:   DEBUGVERIFY(nxrmutex_unlock(&heap->mm_lock));
228: }

232:  *
233:  * Description:
234:  *   Initialize the selected heap data structures, providing the initial
235:  *   heap region.
236:  *
237:  * Input Parameters:

248: void mm_initialize_heap(FAR const struct mm_heap_config_s *config,
249:                         FAR struct mm_heap_s **heap)
250: {
251:   FAR const char *name = config->name;
252:   FAR void *heapstart = config->start;
253:   size_t heapsize = config->size;
254:   int i;
255: 
256:   minfo("Heap: name=%s, start=%p size=%zu\n", name, heapstart, heapsize);
257: 
258:   if (!config->allocheap)
259:     {
260:       /* First ensure the memory to be used is aligned */
261: 
262:       uintptr_t heap_adj = MM_ALIGN_UP((uintptr_t)heapstart);
263:       heapsize -= heap_adj - (uintptr_t)heapstart;
264: 
265:       /* Reserve a block space for mm_heap_s context */
266: 
267:       DEBUGASSERT(heapsize > sizeof(struct mm_heap_s));
268:       *heap = (FAR struct mm_heap_s *)heap_adj;
269:       heapsize -= sizeof(struct mm_heap_s);
270:       heapstart = (FAR char *)heap_adj + sizeof(struct mm_heap_s);
271: 
272:       DEBUGASSERT(MM_MIN_CHUNK >= MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE);
273: 
274:       memset(*heap, 0, sizeof(struct mm_heap_s));
275:       (*heap)->mm_curused = sizeof(struct mm_heap_s);
276:     }
277:   else
278:     {
279:       *heap = lib_memalign(MM_ALIGN, sizeof(struct mm_heap_s));
280:       DEBUGASSERT(*heap != NULL);
281: 
282:       memset(*heap, 0, sizeof(struct mm_heap_s));
283:     }
284: 
285:   (*heap)->mm_nokasan = config->nokasan;
286: 
287:   /* Initialize the node array */
288: 
289:   for (i = 1; i < MM_NNODES; i++)
290:     {
291:       (*heap)->mm_nodelist[i - 1].flink = &(*heap)->mm_nodelist[i];
292:       (*heap)->mm_nodelist[i].blink     = &(*heap)->mm_nodelist[i - 1];
293:     }
294: 
295:   /* Initialize the malloc mutex to one (to support one-at-
296:    * a-time access to private data sets).
297:    */
298: 
299:   nxrmutex_init(&(*heap)->mm_lock);
300: 
301:   /* Add the initial region of memory to the heap */
302: 
303:   mm_addregion(*heap, heapstart, heapsize);
304: 
305: #if defined(CONFIG_FS_PROCFS) && !defined(CONFIG_FS_PROCFS_EXCLUDE_MEMINFO)
306: #  if defined(CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT) || defined(__KERNEL__)
307:   (*heap)->mm_procfs = procfs_register_meminfo(name, *heap, NULL, NULL);
308: #  endif
309: #endif

167:  *
168:  * Description:
169:  *  Find the smallest chunk that satisfies the request. Take the memory from
170:  *  that chunk, save the remaining, smaller chunk (if any).
171:  *
172:  *  8-byte alignment of the allocated data is assured.
173:  *
174:  ****************************************************************************/
175: 
176: FAR void *mm_malloc(FAR struct mm_heap_s *heap, size_t size)
177: {
178:   FAR struct mm_freenode_s *node;
179:   size_t alignsize;
180:   size_t nodesize;
181:   FAR void *ret = NULL;
182:   bool bypass;
183:   int ndx;
184:

186: 
187:   free_delaylist(heap, false);

189: #ifdef CONFIG_MM_HEAP_MEMPOOL
190:   if (heap->mm_mpool)
191:     {
192:       ret = mempool_multiple_alloc(heap->mm_mpool, size);
193:       if (ret != NULL)
194:         {
195:           return ret;
196:         }
197:     }
198: #endif
199: 
200:   /* Adjust the size to account for (1) the size of the allocated node and
201:    * (2) to make sure that it is aligned with MM_ALIGN and its size is at
202:    * least MM_MIN_CHUNK.
203:    */
204: 
205:   if (size < MM_MIN_CHUNK - MM_ALLOCNODE_OVERHEAD)
206:     {
207:       size = MM_MIN_CHUNK - MM_ALLOCNODE_OVERHEAD;
208:     }
209: 
210:   alignsize = MM_ALIGN_UP(size + MM_ALLOCNODE_OVERHEAD);
211:   if (alignsize < size)
212:     {
213:       /* There must have been an integer overflow */
214: 
215:       return NULL;
216:     }
217: 
218:   DEBUGASSERT(alignsize >= MM_ALIGN);
219: 
220:   /* We need to hold the MM mutex while we muck with the nodelist. */
221: 
222:   DEBUGVERIFY(nxrmutex_lock(&heap->mm_lock));
223:   bypass = kasan_bypass(true);
224: 
225:   /* Convert the request size into a nodelist index */
226: 
227:   ndx = mm_size2ndx(alignsize);
228: 
229:   /* Search for a large enough chunk in the list of nodes. This list is
230:    * ordered by size, but will have occasional zero sized nodes as we visit
231:    * other mm_nodelist[] entries.
232:    */
233: 
234:   for (node = heap->mm_nodelist[ndx].flink; node; node = node->flink)
235:     {
236:       DEBUGASSERT(node->blink->flink == node);
237:       nodesize = MM_SIZEOF_NODE(node);
238:       if (nodesize >= alignsize)
239:         {
240:           break;
241:         }
242:     }
243: 
244:   /* If we found a node with non-zero size, then this is one to use. Since
245:    * the list is ordered, we know that it must be the best fitting chunk
246:    * available.
247:    */
248: 
249:   if (node)
250:     {
251:       FAR struct mm_freenode_s *remainder;
252:       FAR struct mm_freenode_s *next;
253:       size_t remaining;
254: 
255:       /* Remove the node.  There must be a predecessor, but there may not be

257:        */
258: 
259:       DEBUGASSERT(node->blink);
260:       node->blink->flink = node->flink;
261:       if (node->flink)

263:           node->flink->blink = node->blink;
264:         }
265: 
266:       /* Get a pointer to the next node in physical memory */
267: 
268:       next = (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)(((FAR char *)node) + nodesize);
269: 
270:       /* Node next must be alloced, otherwise it should be merged.
271:        * Its prenode(the founded node) must be free and preceding should

273:        */
274: 
275:       DEBUGASSERT(MM_NODE_IS_ALLOC(next) && MM_PREVNODE_IS_FREE(next) &&
276:                   next->preceding == nodesize);
277: 
278:       /* Check if we have to split the free node into one of the allocated
279:        * size and another smaller freenode.  In some cases, the remaining
280:        * bytes can be smaller (they may be MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE).  In that
281:        * case, we will just carry the few wasted bytes at the end of the

283:        */
284: 
285:       remaining = nodesize - alignsize;
286:       if (remaining >= MM_MIN_CHUNK)

289:

295:           /* Adjust the size of the node under consideration */

142: void mm_forcefree(FAR struct mm_heap_s *heap, FAR void *mem)
143: {
144:   FAR struct mm_freenode_s *node;
145:   FAR struct mm_freenode_s *prev;
146:   FAR struct mm_freenode_s *next;
147:   size_t nodesize;
148:   size_t prevsize;
149:   bool bypass;
150: 
151:   /* Free mempool blk first */
152: 
153: #ifdef CONFIG_MM_HEAP_MEMPOOL
154:   if (heap->mm_mpool && mempool_multiple_free(heap->mm_mpool, mem) >= 0)
155:     {
156:       return;
157:     }
158: #endif
159: 
160:   DEBUGVERIFY(nxrmutex_lock(&heap->mm_lock));
161:   bypass = kasan_bypass(true);
162:   nodesize = mm_malloc_size(heap, mem);
163: #ifdef CONFIG_MM_FILL_ALLOCATIONS
164:   memset(mem, MM_FREE_MAGIC, nodesize);
165: #endif
166:   kasan_poison(mem, nodesize);
167: 
168:   /* Map the memory chunk into a free node */
169: 
170:   node = (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)
171:          ((FAR char *)kasan_clear_tag(mem) - MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE);
172:   nodesize = MM_SIZEOF_NODE(node);
173: #ifdef CONFIG_MM_RECORD_STACK
174:   backtrace_remove(node->stack);
175: #endif
176: 
177:   /* Sanity check against double-frees */
178: 
179:   if (MM_NODE_IS_ALLOC(node))
180:     {
181:       mm_trace_diag(DIAG_MM_FREE_FAIL, "address:%p, reason:%s",
182:                     mem, "double-free");
183:     }
184: 
185:   DEBUGASSERT(MM_NODE_IS_ALLOC(node));
186:   node->size &= ~MM_ALLOC_BIT;
187: 
188:   /* Update heap statistics */
189: 
190:   heap->mm_curused -= nodesize;
191:   sched_note_heap(NOTE_HEAP_FREE, heap, mem, nodesize, heap->mm_curused);
192: 
193:   /* Check if the following node is free and, if so, merge it */
194: 
195:   next = (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)((FAR char *)node + nodesize);
196:   DEBUGASSERT(MM_PREVNODE_IS_ALLOC(next));
197:   if (MM_NODE_IS_FREE(next))
198:     {
199:       FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *andbeyond;
200:       size_t nextsize = MM_SIZEOF_NODE(next);
201: 
202:       /* Get the node following the next node (which will
203:        * become the new next node). We know that we can never
204:        * index past the tail chunk because it is always allocated.
205:        */
206: 
207:       andbeyond = (FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *)((FAR char *)next + nextsize);
208:       DEBUGASSERT(MM_PREVNODE_IS_FREE(andbeyond) &&
209:                   andbeyond->preceding == nextsize);
210: 
211:       /* Remove the next node.  There must be a predecessor,
212:        * but there may not be a successor node.
213:        */
214: 
215:       DEBUGASSERT(next->blink);
216:       next->blink->flink = next->flink;
217:       if (next->flink)
218:         {
219:           next->flink->blink = next->blink;
220:         }
221: 
222:       /* Then merge the two chunks */
223: 
224:       nodesize            += nextsize;
225:       node->size           = nodesize | (node->size & MM_MASK_BIT);
226:       andbeyond->preceding = nodesize;
227:       next                 = (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)andbeyond;
228:     }
229:   else
230:     {
231:       next->size     |= MM_PREVFREE_BIT;
232:       next->preceding = nodesize;
233:     }
234: 
235:   /* Check if the preceding node is also free and, if so, merge
236:    * it with this node
237:    */
238: 
239:   if (MM_PREVNODE_IS_FREE(node))
240:     {
241:       prev = (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)
242:         ((FAR char *)node - node->preceding);
243:       prevsize = MM_SIZEOF_NODE(prev);
244:       DEBUGASSERT(MM_NODE_IS_FREE(prev) && node->preceding == prevsize);
245: 
246:       /* Remove the node.  There must be a predecessor, but there may
247:        * not be a successor node.
248:        */
249:

53:                 FAR void *arg)
54: {

56:   FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *prev;
57:   size_t nodesize;
58:   bool bypass;
59:   bool locked = false;
60: #if CONFIG_MM_REGIONS > 1
61:   int region;
62: #else
63: #  define region 0
64: #endif
65: 
66:   DEBUGASSERT(handler);
67: 
68:   /* Visit each region */
69: 
70: #if CONFIG_MM_REGIONS > 1
71:   for (region = 0; region < heap->mm_nregions; region++)
72: #endif
73:     {
74:       prev = NULL;
75: 
76:       /* Visit each node in the region
77:        * Retake the mutex for each region to reduce latencies
78:        */
79: 
80: #if defined(CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT) || defined(__KERNEL__)
81:       if (up_interrupt_context())
82:         {
83: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
84:           return;
85: #else

87:             {
88:               return;
89:             }
90: #endif
91:         }
92:       else
93:         {
94:           DEBUGASSERT(!sched_idletask());
95:           DEBUGVERIFY(nxrmutex_lock(&heap->mm_lock));
96:           locked = true;
97:         }
98: #else
99:       /* User space in kernel build cannot check interrupt context */
100: 
101:       DEBUGVERIFY(nxrmutex_lock(&heap->mm_lock));
102:       locked = true;
103: #endif
104: 
105:       bypass = kasan_bypass(true);
106: 
107:       for (node = heap->mm_heapstart[region];
108:            node < heap->mm_heapend[region];
109:            node = (FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *)((FAR char *)node + nodesize))
110:         {
111:           nodesize = MM_SIZEOF_NODE(node);
112:           DEBUGASSERT(nodesize >= MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE);
113:           minfo("region=%d node=%p size=%zu preceding=%u (%c %c)\n",
114:                 region, node, nodesize, (unsigned int)node->preceding,
115:                 MM_PREVNODE_IS_FREE(node) ? 'F' : 'A',
116:                 MM_NODE_IS_ALLOC(node) ? 'A' : 'F');

122:           prev = node;

126:             region, node, heap->mm_heapend[region]);

**Scope**

No files were modified. I inspected the allocator, mapping and type headers, generated PSRAM partitions, callers, power lifecycle, both BK7236N/BK7239 `bk_idk` documentation copies, and the NuttX private-heap implementation.

No `psram_mem_slab.c`, `psram_mem_slab.h`, `frame_buffer_mapping.h`, or matching allocator symbols exist under either `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_idk` or `/home/mi/vela_competition/vendor_beken/chips/bk7236n/bk_idk`. The duplicated `bk_idk` material is documentation, not duplicated allocator source. Both documents describe the same four pools and API at [BK7236N index.rst](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_idk/docs/bk7236n/en/developer-guide/memory_perf/index.rst:97) and [BK7239 index.rst](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_idk/docs/bk7239/en/developer-guide/memory_perf/index.rst:97). Their claim that `psram_heap_type_t` is in `bk_idk/include/driver/psram_types.h` is stale: that header contains only PSRAM hardware types, ending at [psram_types.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_idk/include/driver/psram_types.h:31). The actual enum is in [media_types.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/components/media_types.h:288).

**Four Pool Mapping**

The enum order and indices are fixed: `USER=0`, `AUDIO=1`, `ENCODE=2`, `YUV/DISPLAY=3`, `MAX=4` ([media_types.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/components/media_types.h:292)).

The generated 8 MiB build map is:

| Pool | Start | Size | End |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| USER | `0x60000000` | `0x19000` = 102,400 | `0x60019000` |
| AUDIO | `0x60019000` | `0x19000` = 102,400 | `0x60032000` |
| ENCODE | `0x60032000` | `0x15e000` = 1,433,600 | `0x60190000` |
| DISPLAY/YUV | `0x60190000` | `0x570000` = 5,701,632 | `0x60700000` |

These definitions are at [ram_regions.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/build/bk7258/app/partitions/ram_regions.h:16). They are exactly contiguous and consume the first `0x700000` bytes of PSRAM; CP/AP heaps begin afterward at lines 24-27. The 16 MiB app-ab map preserves exactly the same four boundaries ([app-ab ram_regions.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/partitions/ram_regions.h:16)).

The linker declares four separate regions using all four `*_ADDR` and `*_SIZE` constants ([bk7258_ap_bsp.ld](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/bk7258_ap_bsp.ld:74)). The C mapping does not use those addresses: it casts fixed `0x60000000` to four adjacent byte arrays ([frame_buffer_mapping.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/frame_buffer_mapping.h:24), [frame_buffer_mapping.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/frame_buffer_mapping.h:30)). It is correct only while:

- USER begins at `0x60000000`.
- Every next address equals the sum of all preceding sizes.
- Every preceding size preserves the alignment required by the allocator.
- There are no intentional gaps.

A native replacement should use each explicit `CONFIG_PSRAM_MEM_SLAB_*_ADDR`, not reproduce this implicit struct arithmetic.

**Legacy Metadata Layout**

The allocator assumes 32-bit pointers and 4-byte words. It repeatedly casts pointers through `uint32_t`, for example during initial sizing, splitting, and merging ([psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:45), [psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:196), [psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:285)).

On that ABI:

```text
Allocated block:
  +0x00 uint32_t corrupt_check = 0x8338
  +0x04 uint32_t size          = total block bytes, including this header
  +0x08 user payload
  header = 8 bytes

Free block:
  +0x00 uint32_t corrupt_check = 0xa55a
  +0x04 uint32_t free_size     = total free extent, including descriptor
  +0x08 fb_block_free *next
  +0x0c fb_block_free *previous
  descriptor = 16 bytes
```

The declarations are at [psram_mem_slab.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/include/psram_mem_slab.h:13), with marker values at [psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:25). Free and used layouts deliberately share the first two 32-bit fields so a used header can become a free descriptor in place.

Initialization places one free descriptor at the exact configured start and computes its extent as `align_down(start + configured_size, 4) - start` ([psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:38)). Despite the comment, the start itself is not aligned upward. Consequently, all starts must already be suitably aligned and each enabled pool must be at least 16 bytes. Up to three bytes at the physical end are discarded.

A request is rounded up to four bytes, then charged an 8-byte used header; total block size is raised to at least 16 bytes so it can later hold a free descriptor ([psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:116)). Thus:

```text
legacy_total = max(align_up(request, 4) + 8, 16)
returned alignment = 4 bytes
malloc(0) consumes 16 bytes and returns an 8-byte payload area
```

**Best Fit, Splitting, and Coalescing**

The free list is kept in ascending physical-address order. Allocation scans the entire list and retains the smallest eligible block, so it is true best fit; equal-size ties retain the first, lowest-address block ([psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:141)).

Allocation is taken from the high-address end of a free extent. Normally the free node remains at the same address and its size is reduced; the used header is written at `free_start + remaining_size` ([psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:199)). If the remainder would be smaller than 16 bytes, the complete free block is consumed ([psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:164)).

There is a deliberate root-sentinel exception. The first free node has `previous == NULL` and is eligible only when at least 16 bytes will remain. Exact or near-exact consumption is permitted only for non-root nodes, and exact removal asserts that `previous != NULL` ([psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:147), [psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:185)). Therefore every pool permanently retains at least its 16-byte root free descriptor. A completely empty initialized pool reports one free extent, not zero free nodes.

Freeing searches all four configured ranges to infer the pool ([psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:259)). It then walks the address-ordered list:

- If the released extent immediately follows a free node, it merges downward into that node and then also merges the next free node if adjacent ([psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:281)).
- If it precedes the current free node, it inserts after `prev_node` and merges with the current node when adjacent ([psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:307)).
- Otherwise it appends after the last free node ([psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:344)).

Coalescing is eager and can combine both neighbors in one free operation. The permanent root makes insertion before the first node “impossible”; that path asserts rather than supporting it.

**API, Statistics, Locking, and Lifecycle**

`bk_psram_frame_buffer_init()` returns no status, clears only the four control arrays, and reconstructs each enabled pool in place ([psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:77)). Calling it with live allocations silently invalidates them.

`malloc(type, size)` returns `NULL` only for exhaustion. An uninitialized pool logs and asserts rather than returning an error ([psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:104)). `free(NULL)` is a no-op ([psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:224)); non-null free has no type argument and discovers the pool by address.

There are no maintained allocation counters, current usage, high-water mark, requested-byte accounting, or formal statistics API. `dump_blocks()` reconstructs free/used information by walking the free list and linearly scanning in-band headers ([psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:363)). Reported used sizes include the 8-byte header and any absorbed tail; free sizes include free descriptors. Its `FB_FREE_PATTERN` “not merged yet” case at lines 483-488 is not a stable post-`free()` state.

Allocation and list mutation disable global interrupts ([psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:131), [psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:255)). This gives task/ISR exclusion only if that macro globally serializes every participating CPU. In an SMP build, local interrupt masking is not a cross-CPU lock. Free also reads and modifies the allocated header before taking the lock at lines 239-256. Initialization is wholly unlocked. Dump holds interrupts disabled while traversing and logging the entire heap, producing potentially extreme interrupt latency.

The sole initialization call is the PSRAM-on callback ([media_service.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_service/src/media_service.c:73), [media_service.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_service/src/media_service.c:115)). The PSRAM-off callback is a no-op. The `bk_idk` docs explicitly say CPU1 startup initializes it and CPU1 shutdown needs no de-registration ([BK7236N index.rst](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_idk/docs/bk7236n/en/developer-guide/memory_perf/index.rst:160)). This assumes all allocations and users disappear before PSRAM power-down and that no stale pointer is used after the next reinitialization.

Only ENCODE and DISPLAY are used by visible callers. They request an extra 32 bytes and manually align frame payloads to 32 bytes ([frame_buffer.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/multimedia/comm/frame_buffer.c:39), [frame_buffer.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/multimedia/comm/frame_buffer.c:41), [frame_buffer.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/multimedia/comm/frame_buffer.c:87)). The allocator itself promises only 4-byte alignment.

**Known Bugs and Unsafe Assumptions**

1. `heap_size[type]` is indexed before validating or reducing `type` modulo four, causing out-of-bounds access for invalid enums ([psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:110)). Later modulo conversion would also wrongly alias invalid types onto valid pools.
2. Request alignment and `size + sizeof(header)` have no overflow checks. Large requests can wrap and receive a dangerously undersized allocation ([psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:118)).
3. All pointer arithmetic truncates through `uint32_t`; it is non-portable to 64-bit address spaces.
4. The allocated marker check is commented out. Free blindly overwrites metadata before validating the pointer, pool, allocation state, or lock ownership ([psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:239)).
5. Double-free can overwrite an active free-list node’s `0xa55a` marker with `0xf00f` before eventually asserting or corrupting the list.
6. Interior, stale, one-past, and arbitrary pointers can be interpreted as headers. Range membership alone does not establish that a pointer was returned by this allocator.
7. Membership accepts `mem_ptr == heap_start + configured_size`, an invalid one-past endpoint ([psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:61)).
8. The mapping ignores explicit addresses and assumes contiguous regions beginning at hard-coded `0x60000000`.
9. Pool starts and sizes are not validated for alignment, minimum size, overlap, arithmetic overflow, PSRAM capacity, or conflicts with subsequent heaps.
10. Local interrupt masking is insufficient SMP protection unless the platform macro implements a real global mechanism. Long best-fit scans and debug logging also make interrupt-disabled latency unbounded by a small constant.
11. Reinitialization and power transitions are not synchronized with allocation/free operations or outstanding owners.
12. The diagnostic scanner trusts corrupt sizes and may skip outside the heap; its 1000-block safeguard applies only to unknown-marker steps, not valid-looking corrupt sizes ([psram_mem_slab.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/media_utils/src/psram_mem_slab.c:440)).

**NuttX-Native Guidance**

Use four independent `struct mm_heap_s *` instances, one per enum value. Do not use one heap with four `mm_addregion()` calls: that would combine statistics and allocation policy and would no longer enforce functional pool boundaries.

Initialize each instance with `mm_initialize(name, explicit_start, explicit_size)` ([NuttX mm.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/include/nuttx/mm/mm.h:274)). With default configuration, NuttX stores `struct mm_heap_s` inside that pool, aligns the remaining region, installs head/tail guards, and creates one free chunk ([mm_initialize.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/mm/mm_heap/mm_initialize.c:248), [mm_initialize.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/mm/mm_heap/mm_initialize.c:153)). Expect usable capacities and returned addresses to differ from the legacy allocator.

Keep the compatibility API, but validate `type < PSRAM_HEAP_MAX` before indexing. Dispatch allocation directly to `mm_malloc(heaps[type], size)`. For untyped free, find exactly one pool using strict half-open boundaries `[start, end)`, verify `mm_heapmember()`, and call `mm_free()` on that heap. NuttX’s membership check itself uses strict guard-node boundaries ([mm_heapmember.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/mm/mm_heap/mm_heapmember.c:58)). Exact-pointer validity remains an API precondition; range membership cannot make arbitrary interior pointers safe.

Select NuttX’s default heap manager if preserving best-fit behavior matters. It searches a size-ordered free list for the smallest satisfactory chunk ([mm_malloc.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/mm/mm_heap/mm_malloc.c:225)), splits only when at least `MM_MIN_CHUNK` remains ([mm_malloc.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/mm/mm_heap/mm_malloc.c:278)), and coalesces both physical neighbors on free ([mm_free.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/mm/mm_heap/mm_free.c:193)). TLSF would preserve isolation and general semantics but not the exact best-fit policy.

NuttX normally provides `MM_ALIGN = 2 * sizeof(uintptr_t)` unless configured otherwise ([NuttX mm.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/include/nuttx/mm/mm.h:165)); its default allocator explicitly guarantees 8-byte data alignment ([mm_malloc.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/mm/mm_heap/mm_malloc.c:166)). Preserve the existing frame-level 32-byte alignment wrapper or replace it with `mm_memalign(heap, 32, size)` after checking whether callers require the separately allocated `frame_buffer_t` prefix.

Use `mm_mallinfo()` per pool for arena, free/allocated chunks, current occupied bytes, largest free chunk, and peak usage ([mm_mallinfo.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/mm/mm_heap/mm_mallinfo.c:129), [malloc.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/include/malloc.h:64)). `mm_heapfree()` and `mm_heapfree_largest()` provide direct free metrics ([mm_mallinfo.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/mm/mm_heap/mm_mallinfo.c:187)). These figures include NuttX allocator overhead, so expose both configured region size and allocator statistics.

Each NuttX heap owns a recursive mutex ([internal mm.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/mm/mm_heap/mm.h:246)); allocation/free lock around metadata changes ([mm_malloc.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/mm/mm_heap/mm_malloc.c:220), [mm_free.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/mm/mm_heap/mm_free.c:160)). This is SMP-safe task-context synchronization, but ordinary `mm_malloc/mm_free` should not be treated as ISR APIs. ISR users should use a preallocated fixed-block pool or defer work to task context.

Finally, keep lifecycle state and its transition lock in internal SRAM, not PSRAM. On orderly shutdown: mark all four pools unavailable, block new calls, quiesce users, verify no live allocations, call `mm_uninitialize()` while PSRAM is still powered, null all handles, then power down. NuttX deinitialization releases delayed frees, KASAN/procfs registration, and the heap mutex but does not prove that callers released every allocation ([mm_initialize.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/mm/mm_heap/mm_initialize.c:393)). After unplanned PSRAM loss, treat every old pointer as invalid and construct four fresh heaps only after power and mapping are restored.
